# RecipeHub is specified through design, and the build is yours

## Brief

- **Audience**: the incoming engineering lead for RecipeHub
- **Occasion**: onboarding briefing in their first week, presented live
- **Decision or action sought**: commit to owning the engineering layers, close the open calls that gate the build, and start the first build step
- **Time slot or page budget**: 20 minutes (10 content slides)
- **Kind**: deck
- **Constraints**: internal; every document is draft, so nothing may be presented as approved; no HELIX or artifact vocabulary on slides
- **Look**: technical
- **Scope**: docs/helix (product vision, requirements, recipe sharing feature spec, database decision record, recipe store technical design)
- **Breadth**: survey
- **Angle**: what a new engineering lead inherits: what the product is, what has been decided, what is still open
- **Must cover**: product vision; the data decision; the recipe sharing feature
- **Must omit**: none
- **Max messages**: 5
- **Takeaway**: RecipeHub is specified through design, and closing four open calls lets you start the build.

## Story

- **Flow**: internal-alignment
- **Takeaway**: RecipeHub is specified through design, and closing four open calls lets you start the build.
- **Messages** (ranked by how much each moves the lead's decision to commit and start):
  1. Four open calls gate the build, and two carry the engineering lead's name (evidence: prd.md#Open Questions, three questions each naming who answers; ADR-001-sqlite.md header table, status Proposed with Engineering as a decider)
  2. A deliberately small stack carries launch: one SQLite file with measured Postgres triggers, one REST API, S3 photos (evidence: ADR-001-sqlite.md#Decision, #Alternatives, #Validation; TD-recipe-store.md#Technical Approach, #Component Changes, #Implementation Sequence)
  3. Six cook actions ship at launch, and recipe sharing is the one that creates the community (evidence: prd.md#Requirements P0 list and #Non-Goals; FEAT-recipe-share.md#Problem Statement, #Requirements, #Constraints and Assumptions)
  4. RecipeHub is an ad-free, mobile-first recipe community for home cooks, specified through five draft documents (evidence: product-vision.md#Mission Statement, #Positioning, #Why Now, #Target Market; prd.md#Users and Scope; the five frontmatter status fields)
  5. Three dated numbers define success, and all read zero today (evidence: product-vision.md#Success Definition; prd.md#Success Metrics)
- **Beats and titles** (titles written before any body):

  | # | Beat | Title (claim) | Message | Exhibit |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | why-we-are-here | RecipeHub is specified through design, and the build is yours | takeaway | title surface, hero marker |
  | 2 | agenda | The survey runs from five draft documents to your first call | all | numbered list, ask at right |
  | 3 | where-we-are | Five draft documents define the recipe app; none is approved | M4 | layer stack of the five documents, database decision highlighted |
  | 4 | what-changed | Home cooks plan on phones while recipe sites sell ads | M4 | statement, one supporting sentence |
  | 5 | where-we-are-going | Home cooks get one trusted, ad-free place for recipes | M4 | today versus RecipeHub, four parallel rows |
  | 6 | where-we-are-going | Six cook actions ship at launch; only posting creates content | M3 | five-step cook journey, posting highlighted |
  | 7 | where-we-are-going | One form and one photo publish a cook's recipe | M3 | three panels: authoring, visibility, feedback |
  | 8 | how-we-get-there | One SQLite file carries recipes until a trigger brings Postgres | M2 | timeline from today to a Postgres migration |
  | 9 | how-we-get-there | The build puts recipes in SQLite and photos in S3 | M2 | five-step data path, storage service highlighted |
  | 10 | what-it-means-for-you | Four open calls gate the build and two are yours | M1 | table of roles, first calls, and what each blocks |

The deck script is written and gated by hand. Nothing further can be verified in this session, so here is the hand-off.

**Deliverable**: `docs/helix/06-iterate/deliverables/DEL-001-engineering-lead-survey.md`, status draft, flow `internal-alignment`, look `technical`, 10 content slides for the 20-minute slot. HELIX was activated from the `.helix.yml` marker at autonomy `high`, with the catalog bound from the source checkout at `/Users/erik/Projects/helix/workflows` since the project has no in-tree catalog.

**Takeaway**: RecipeHub is specified through design, and closing four open calls lets you start the build.

**Titles-only outline**
1. RecipeHub is specified through design, and the build is yours
2. The survey runs from five draft documents to your first call
3. Five draft documents define the recipe app; none is approved
4. Home cooks plan on phones while recipe sites sell ads
5. Home cooks get one trusted, ad-free place for recipes
6. Six cook actions ship at launch; only posting creates content
7. One form and one photo publish a cook's recipe
8. One SQLite file carries recipes until a trigger brings Postgres
9. The build puts recipes in SQLite and photos in S3
10. Four open calls gate the build and two are yours
11. Three dated numbers decide whether the build succeeded
12. Close the four calls, then start the build at the schema
13. Sources appendix

The three must-cover concepts land on slides 4 to 5 (vision), 8 (data decision), and 7 (recipe sharing). The inventory produced 15 concept groups; 14 are covered and the technology stack is omitted to speaker notes for budget.

**Findings worth acting on before the briefing**
- The decision record says no database has been selected, while the technical design says auth and read-only browse endpoints already exist on SQLite. The deck raises this on slide 3 and in the ask rather than resolving it. It belongs in an alignment pass on those two documents.
- No engineering owner is recorded anywhere. The ADR names engineering as a co-decider but has sat in Proposed since May. The ask assigns the incoming lead by inference.
- Five documents are referenced but absent: the parking lot, user stories, the ratings and comments features, and a runbook.

**Gate status**
- The mechanical checker could not be run: shell execution of scripts outside the project directory needs an approval this non-interactive session cannot grant. I applied its rules by hand from its source. That caught two rule-of-three titles, three over-length titles, a caption and a bullet ending in reversals, an ask band restating its title, and five title pairs sharing no content word. All are fixed and recorded under Story and Render.
- No `.pptx` or `.pdf` was produced, as the request stated rendering is unavailable. The Render section names the missing tools.
- Ask dates of 22 and 29 September 2026 are proposals one and two weeks out, sourced to the Assumptions section, not to any governing document.

**Next**: re-run `check-deliverable.py` and the renderer on a host that permits them, then have a person review before the status moves off draft.
